title: add-ci-change-visualizer-and-dep-curation-refactor
author: Amaya Chen
release_notes: Add lightweight CI Change Visualizer and Go-based dependency curation tool; refactor GitHub Actions to emit a change-manifest and simplify lint/test profiles. No runtime/API breaking changes.
description: Context: Our lint/test GitHub Actions have become difficult to reason about for large cross-repo changes and dependency rotations. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a small CI Change Visualizer service that consumes a machine-readable CI change manifest and provides a compact view of what pipeline lanes will execute for a given PR, and (2) a Go-based dependency curation tool that analyzes deps updated by bots and suggests a curated whitelist with reasons. Motivation: faster triage during dependency upgrades, fewer flaky reruns due to unexpected matrix combinations, and a repeatable path to approve bulk dep updates. What this PR does: - Add .github/actions/manifest-generator action that runs early in the PR pipeline and outputs a ci-change-manifest.json artifact describing which lint/test lanes will run given modified paths and changed packages. - Introduce tools/ci-visualizer: a tiny Go web service (single binary) that can render manifests locally or as a lightweight cluster tool for SRE to inspect PRs; includes an offline static renderer (SVG) for embedding in release notes. - Add go/cmd/dep-curator: CLI that ingests dependabot/renovate PRs, computes surface area (impacted packages, transitive surface, test coverage risk), and emits a curated suggestions file used by release engineers. - Refactor GitHub Actions to consume the manifest: reduce redundant matrix expansions, split heavy integration lanes to a nightly fallback, and consolidate lint profiles into three deterministic shards (fast, medium, full). - Add docs/ci/visualizer.md and small Makefile targets for running the visualizer locally. Rollout plan and safety: - Feature gated behind a repo-level opt-in label (ci-visualize) for initial two-week rollout. - Manifest-generator added as a non-blocking early step; it is allowed to fail non-fatally and will be hardened in a follow-up. - Dep-curator runs only in periodic release jobs and as an opt-in guardian on large dependency PRs. Checklist: - [x] Add manifest-generator action and unit tests - [x] Implement visualizer CLI + static render mode - [x] Implement dep-curator analysis and report generation - [x] Wire updated workflows to read manifest and reduce matrix size - [x] Add docs and runbook for on-call - [x] Manual dogfood: ran visualizer against last 30 merged PRs and verified output - [x] Added integration test that validates manifest -> workflow decision mapping Tests and validation: - Local unit tests for manifest-generator (path matching rules), dep-curator heuristics, and visualizer rendering. - End-to-end CI smoke run in a feature branch with sample manifest artifacts. - Load test for visualizer: 500 concurrent static render requests locally (baseline latency < 120ms). Related work: ENG-2331 (ci manifest design), ENG-2332 (dep curation heuristics), PM-405 (release UX improvements). This PR intentionally avoids changing the runtime build or the hosted API paths; it focuses on repo hygiene and developer feedback loops. Next steps: automate curator suggestions as a bot comment on large dep PRs and add a small dashboard for historical dep churn.

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Nice approach. Can we guarantee manifest generation is deterministic across runners? Please add a hash to the artifact to detect drift.
Amaya Chen: Added deterministic serialization and content-hash to the manifest. See commit 3.
Linnea Sørensen: Dep-curator heuristics look good but please document the false-positive rate and add a confidence score to the report.
Amaya Chen: Added confidence score and updated docs with expected FP rate (~8% observed in historical sample).
Marco Ruiz: The workflow changes reduce matrix runs but we should ensure nightly integration still covers the trimmed combinations. Recommend adding a nightly fallback matrix job.
Amaya Chen: Added nightly/integration-fallback workflow and verified it runs in the scheduled pipeline.
CI Bot: build passed on ubuntu-latest (node, go), lint passed, integration smoke failed on first run due to flaky test X; rerun succeeded.
Ravi Patel: Approving pending minor doc nit fixes.
Marco Ruiz: Approved and will monitor during rollout.
notes_for_oncall: The visualizer exposes an HTTP status endpoint at /health; instrumented Prometheus metrics under /metrics.
If manifest generation starts failing, the non-blocking opt-in label prevents CI breaks; look at action logs under Actions -> manifest-generator.
Dep-curator is safe-run only for now; if curator starts posting suggestions automatically, there will be a feature flag in admin settings.
